calls.body: The Rangers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Senators are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Senators’ defense.

calls.body: The Rangers are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Senators are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Rangers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.

calls.head: The Senators want Batherson away from the big guns
calls.body: At home, the Senators keep sending Batherson’s line (Foegele, Cozens and Batherson) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Travis Green has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Rangers’ third line is Cuylle, Laba and Tolvanen.
calls.call: The Senators’ L2 (Foegele, Cozens and Batherson) spends at least 35% of its 5-on-5 time against the Rangers’ third line, against about 25% with no line matching.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 60% chance, and they delivered.

NYR.head: We had the Rangers as slight underdogs (40%), and it went Ottawa’s way.

surprises.head: Ottawa found the good looks for once
surprises.body: The Rangers usually allow fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Not tonight: Ottawa’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.5% (about 6.2% against the Rangers) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 80 games.

story.head: Batherson lights the lamp for a hat trick
paras: Drake Batherson and Tim Stützle scored just over a minute apart early in the first to put the Senators up 2-0. The second period brought five goals. Batherson scored his second of the night early in the period to make it 3-0, but Will Cuylle got the Rangers on the board shorthanded midway through the period. Dylan Cozens made it 4-1 for the Sens a little over a minute later. J.T. Miller cut Ottawa’s lead to 4-2 a minute and a half later, and Alexis Lafrenière made it 4-3 with 26 seconds left in the second. It was a busy third period. Jake Sanderson stretched the lead to 5-3 with less than seven minutes left, but Pavel Dorofeyev pulled the Rangers within one with four and a half minutes left. Michael Amadio ended any hope of a comeback with an empty-netter with a little over a minute left. Batherson completed his hat trick into the empty net with 12 seconds left. Sanderson finished with a goal and two assists.

The chances were closer than the score. Jonas Johansson made 24 saves for the Senators, and Dylan Garand allowed five goals on 22 shots. The Senators improved to 8-4-0 and climbed to second in the Atlantic, while the Rangers dropped to 7-5-1, second in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Tim Stützle has a point in four straight games, with a goal in each of the last three.
The Rangers have gone winless in five straight on the road.
Dylan Cozens scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 15 (eleven games played since).
Three of the preview’s four calls held.
